items.title: Two trains collide in Egypt, killing 7 people and injuring more than 100, authorities say
items.brief: At least seven people were killed and 112 people injured after two trains collided in Egypt on Sunday, the country’s health ministry said.

items.title: Pope Leo urges President Milei, a Trump ally, to ‘safeguard democracy’ on arrival in Argentina
items.brief: Pope Leo XIV has called on Argentine President Javier Milei and the country’s political leaders to “safeguard democracy” and demonstrate a “careful use of words” during his first speech in Buenos Aires.

items.title: Building owned by Saudi oil giant damaged in missile attack on Riyadh’s financial district
items.brief: A building belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco in the financial district of the capital Riyadh has been damaged in a missile attack.

items.title: Trump says renewed attacks on Iran ‘highly unlikely’ if talks show progress

items.title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over foreign intelligence concerns
items.brief: Nvidia announced Sunday it is launching an independent investigation into its chief executive and founder, Jensen Huang, over concerns he was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”

items.title: Police make arrest in a deadly shooting at Winston-Salem State during homecoming weekend
items.brief: Authorities on Sunday arrested a man in a shooting during homecoming weekend at Winston-Salem State University in North Carolina that left one person dead and at least one other person injured.

items.title: Poland stunned as suspect with far-right views kills 6 in Kraków mass shooting
items.brief: Poland has been left shocked after a rare mass shooting in the country’s south — prompting national mourning and heightened security, as authorities say the attack was likely driven by far-right ideology.
